items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-09
items.q: There's a little boy in London, Eddie Calvin. I don't think he gets a high note over a deal, but what he plays means so much.

ctx.x: And we gave a whole lounge. Do you find, uh, like, uh, some chance of, uh, having some of our typical Latin music, uh, played in the jazz form, uh, improvising? Yeah.

Easy. Easy. Easy. You can improvise any music. And it would sound so much good if you have nice thoughts about it. Don't yanky-tanky hit, you know. Yeah. Yanky-tanky-tanky. I mean, just play it. You know. Nobody knows the trouble of seeing. I mean, if you swing it, it sounds touching. That's not the piece so much, isn't it? The, the musician that gets the high day, he's got to ham it up. And to me, I think a musician inferior that can't play nothing decent. He's trying to get away from something. We play Tiger…
I love my baby, you know what I mean? Yes, it's a, we can provide, but don't try to drown it.
